clue.text: Girl foreshortened by painter

indicators.note: foreshortened means drawn shorter, so the painter's name loses its tail end

parts.note: John Bellany was a Scottish painter

explanation.surface: A portrait of a young woman comes out squashed in the hands of an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreshortened' cuts the last two letters, NY, from BELLANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Bella is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl in crosswords.

clue.text: It's an American trap to put a fashionable young man on the panel

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a buck is an old word for a dandy
a board is a panel, of wood or of people

explanation.surface: A trendy youth is tricked onto a committee in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trap' is a light horse-drawn carriage, not a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckboard is a simple four-wheeled horse cart from the United States; a trap is a small carriage.

clue.text: Vessel in R Nile coming to grief

indicators.note: coming to grief means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship sinks on the river Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship, a kind of sea vessel.

clue.text: Human skill provided diamonds by trickery

parts.note: art is human skill as opposed to nature
if means provided, on condition that
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A craftsman offers jewels through clever deception.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is cunning deception used to fool people.

clue.text: One who will understand if you lose your voice

definitions.text: One who will understand if you lose your voice

parts.words: One who will understand if you lose your voice
parts.note: a person who follows speech by watching the mouth needs no sound at all, so a voiceless speaker is still understood

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sympathetic friend when you have laryngitis; the real reading is someone who never needed to hear you.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person interprets speech from mouth movements, so silent words are still understood.

clue.text: Lakme's opening song in a place of seclusion

indicators.note: opening picks the starting letter of Lakme's

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: An aria from Delibes' opera Lakme is sung in a hidden retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a hideaway or den where one withdraws from others.

clue.text: Looking for cups in drug investigation

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
hunting, a search, is a kind of investigation

explanation.surface: Police seek trophies during a narcotics inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot-hunting is chasing trophies or prizes, sporting cups being the classic prize.

clue.text: The moral values of a lisping Queen's favourite

indicators.note: a lisper turns every S into a TH, so we want the name as such a speaker would pronounce it

parts.note: the Earl of Essex was a favourite of Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: Moral standards of a royal courtier with a speech defect.
explanation.walkthrough: Say ESSEX with a lisp and it comes out roughly as 'eth-ix'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics are the principles of right and wrong that guide conduct.

clue.text: Coalition supporting Democratic delay

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: an alliance is a coalition

explanation.surface: A coalition backs the Democrats in stalling.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance can mean dawdling or wasting time, so it is a kind of lingering.

clue.text: Defence managed without notes

indicators.note: without means outside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
E and D are musical notes

explanation.surface: A team defended without any music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside, its old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A redan is a V-shaped fortification, part of a fortress's protective works.

clue.text: Soldiers leave snake to choke

indicators.note: the soldiers leave, that is they are taken out of the snake's name

parts.note: a boa constrictor is a snake that squeezes its prey
OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops abandon a snake that is about to throttle them.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrict is to squeeze tight, which is how one would strangle or choke.

clue.text: Robust daughter drawn

parts.note: robust means hale, healthy and strong

explanation.surface: A healthy girl is sketched by an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' suggests a picture or a tired face; here it means pulled along.
explanation.definitionFit: Haled is an old word for hauled or dragged, the past tense of a verb of pulling.

clue.text: Fellow in cloth cap is deprived

indicators.note: in tells us the fellow sits within the cap

parts.note: a beret is a soft round cloth cap

explanation.surface: A man in a flat cap is down on his luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bereft means being left without something, so it matches lacking or being robbed of it.

clue.text: Perform official duty

definitions.meaning: to work or operate, as a machine does its job
a formal occasion or the role someone holds

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to operate; as a noun it means a role or formal ceremony.

clue.text: Volunteer the leech was brought in to treat?

definitions.text: Volunteer the leech was brought in to treat?

parts.words: Volunteer the leech was brought in to treat?
parts.note: a medical leech draws blood; one who gives blood willingly is pictured as the leech's patient

explanation.definitionFit: Someone giving blood freely is a volunteer whose blood is drawn, as a leech would draw it.

clue.text: Express lorry you heard at night

parts.note: an artic is a British ... lorry, a cab towing a trailer

indicators.note: heard says the word you is taken by its sound alone, a single letter

parts.note: the word you is spoken like the letter U
late can mean far into the evening, so at night

explanation.surface: A fast truck you hear rumbling past after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a description of the lorry, but it is the verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate is to put thoughts into clear words, which is to express them.

clue.text: Legal document fully illustrated in What Katy Did at School

definitions.text: Legal document fully illustrated in What Katy Did at School

parts.words: Legal document fully illustrated in What Katy Did at School
parts.note: the book name is a heading, and 'what Katy did' is an act she performed; put them together and you have a property paper

explanation.walkthrough: What Katy Did at School is a classic children's book by Susan Coolidge; the clue splits it into a heading and an action.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the document proving ownership of property, a legal record.

clue.text: Responsibility for executing commission

parts.note: the burden of carrying out a task one has been given, read straight as a phrase

explanation.definitionFit: The word means the burden of a duty placed on someone, such as carrying out an assignment.

clue.text: Firm words in keynote address

parts.note: set means firm or fixed
speech is spoken words

explanation.surface: A strong statement in a major lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A set speech is a prepared formal oration, like the main talk at a conference.

clue.text: A 5-cent piece, or any copper penny that's for tipping

indicators.note: for tipping means to be tipped over, so the pieces are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: CU is the chemical symbol for copper
IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Any small copper coin will do as a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for tipping' jumbles ANY, CU, P and IE. A picayune was an old coin in the southern US worth about five cents.
explanation.definitionFit: The picayune was a small coin of low value used in the American South, worth half a dime.

clue.text: Customs Frederick was a slave to

definitions.meaning: in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Pirates of Penzance, Frederic is the 'slave of' this, an obligation he feels bound by

explanation.walkthrough: The Pirates of Penzance is subtitled The Slave of Duty; the hero Frederic is bound by obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a levy on goods and a moral obligation, the thing Frederic serves.

clue.text: Clashing with a business event?

parts.note: CO, company, is a business
an incident is an event or occurrence

explanation.surface: Two corporate functions booked for the same date collide.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that clash in time happen together, so they are simultaneous.

clue.text: A hole in the heart — or a stomach in a state? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the clue claims the stomach goes in the state, but just the opposite means the state goes in the stomach

parts.note: tum is a colloquial word for stomach
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A heart defect, or perhaps a nervous stomach caused by anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a stomach in a state' reads like nerves; 'Just the opposite' tells you to put the state inside the stomach instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is one of the upper chambers of the heart, a cavity in it.

clue.text: Regular diet broken late in the day

parts.note: regular means even, steady

indicators.note: broken says the letters of diet are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their steady eating plan in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is an old poetic word for evening, the close of the day.

clue.text: Grind down points at either end of stick.

indicators.note: at either end of means the points flank the stick on both sides

parts.note: E is a compass point; two of them here
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: Sharpen a stick by grinding its tips.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as water grinds rock.

clue.text: Almost became an international, but wildly impulsive

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut just short of its final letter

parts.note: made can mean became, as in 'she made a fine captain'
a cap is a player selected for a national side, and the honour itself

explanation.surface: A footballer very nearly earned national selection but threw it away by being reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last E from MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap person acts on reckless whims, behaving with wild abandon.

clue.text: Furniture to carry aloft

definitions.meaning: to lift someone on others' shoulders in triumph

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a seat and also the act of carrying a hero shoulder-high.

clue.text: Refuse to leave bird island

annotationWithheld.why: Refuse to leave bird island (4): INCH is a Scottish word for island, but no reading of 'Refuse to leave bird' gives INCH from a bird such as FINCH without 'refuse' giving F, which it does not.

clue.text: Strobe lighting reveals signs of corruption

indicators.note: reveals says the answer is on show inside the words strobe lighting

explanation.surface: Flashing lights expose evidence of decay.
explanation.walkthrough: Obeli (plural of obelus) are dagger marks used by editors to flag a passage as spurious or corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors print these dagger marks beside passages they judge spurious, so the marks flag textual corruption.

clue.text: Sister meeting copperhead has to make her will orally!

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
split as copper and head: CU is the chemical symbol for copper and pate means head

explanation.surface: A nun meets a venomous snake and hastily dictates her last wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copperhead' looks like the snake, but splits into copper (CU) and head (PATE).
explanation.definitionFit: To nuncupate is to declare a testament by spoken word rather than in writing.

clue.text: Moped with horn disturbed stout, party

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A scooter's hooter wakes up a plump fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges MOPED and HORN. A 'stout party' is an old jokey phrase for a fat person.
explanation.definitionFit: An endomorph is a person with a heavy, rounded build, a portly individual.

clue.text: The conductor needs to get down to it

definitions.text: The conductor needs to get down to it

parts.words: The conductor needs to get down to it
parts.note: an electrical conductor is connected to the ground for safety, and 'down to' this is an idiom for being practical

explanation.definitionFit: Electrical wiring is grounded to the soil, and the planet's ground is what we come down to.
